steps.text: Place the soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, orange juice, sweet chili sauce, chili-garlic sauce, garlic, and curry powder in a large plastic zipper bag. Seal and knead the bag with your fingers to mix all the ingredients and dissolve the sugar. Place the chicken thighs into the marinade, squeeze out the air from the bag, zip the bag closed, and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-low heat; lightly oil the grate.
Remove the chicken from the bag, pour the excess marinade into a small saucepan, and bring to a full boil for about 1 minute to sterilize the marinade.
Grill the chicken thighs until they are no longer pink in the middle and show grill marks, about 25 minutes, basting them generously with the sterilized marinade as they grill.

raw_recipe.headline: Asian Grilled Chicken
raw_recipe.description: The flavorful marinade for these grilled chicken thighs is a little sweet, a little salty, and a little tangy, with a hint of spice from Asian chili sauce, curry, and garlic.

video.description: See how to make a quick-and-easy marinade for tender grilled chicken thighs.

review.reviewBody: Wow...what a delicious marinade for chicken. I used chicken breasts, just because that's what we prefer, and marinated it only for two hours because I ran out of time and the flavors still came through beautifully. I loved the sweet chili sauce and the spicy chili sauce all rolled into one. I made this with Thai Pineapple Fried Rice (one of our lovely Buzz lady's personal recipe) and it made a perfect meal. This will be a definite repeat meal in my house!

Made as written, but (purposely) increased curry to 1 tsp, and (accidentally) increased sriracha to 1 tablespoon. Marinated boneless thighs overnight, grilled for 12 minutes total over medium heat, wrapped in foil, and let rest for 10 minutes. Fantastic! The second time I made these, I served them with a batch of Lime Cilantro Rice from this site... *chef's kiss* ...the perfect compliment.

We loved this recipe. Omitted the sweet chili sauce I didn't have. Everything else I had. I added a drizzle of sesame oil in the marinade. Let it set all day in fridge. Served with ALL Recipes coconut rice recipe and oven roasted green beans.

This had a nice citrus flavor. I couldn't find any Thai sweet chili sauce, so I increased the chili garlic sauce and added a Tbsp of honey for sweetness. I'm allergic to curry, so I left that out. I used split skinless breasts and sautéed them on the stove. They were very moist and flavorful. We will definitely have these again.

This is insanely good! I added a tbl of honey to marinade. I marinated chicken breasts 6 hours, reserved the marinade, boiled for 3 min to sterilize, brushed it on chicken as the filleted boneless skinless chicken breasts were grilling, and it was insane. I cooked my chicken 4 min each side at 400 grill temp that was plenty. I used the remaining sauce for dipping and over rice and vegetables. I will make it again and again!

AH-mazing! I make this all the time and the family loves it! I follow the recipe exactly. I make extra marinade and then boil it and add corn starch for a gravy. Serve with jasmine rice and broccoli or snow peas. Delicious!

Made as written with an addition of lime zest and a bit of olive oil in the marinade. I used all chicken drumsticks, I liked the bit of heat/spice. It had good flavor and will be made again. It's best to boil the leftover marinade for 5 minutes to be completely safe.

I made this for supper last night. I tried to make as written but I was out of curry powder and my lime only gave me 1 tbsp of juice. It was very good! I marinated for 3 hrs and kept some marinade aside and thickened as others suggested. It was delicious fresh but today it was fantastic. The marinade had time to blend flavors. I added it to my chicken and vegetables when I reheated it for lunch. I just wish I had rice to go with it. I can’t wait to see how it tastes when I have proper amount of lime juice and curry powder. Thank you for the wonderful recipe. It’s a keeper!!

WOW! I'm so excited! I made the sauce as directed, except for adding a tad more brown sugar. I wanted to use the meat for a stir fry, so I thinly sliced chicken breast and marinated for about 6 hours. I cooked up half the batch for dinner and it was pretty good. Not restaurant quality, but tasty. Then I let the other meat marinate another day. I looked online for some tips to make my meat more tender and juicy and I finally found it (I've been searching for YEARS). The key is to cook the chicken on high heat in very small batches so the meat sears and caramelizes instead of boiling in the juices. The first time I cooked all the meat at one time. The second time I cooked in small batches and it was AMAZING!!! Absolutely restaurant quality and this marinade makes it so delicious. I will use this again and again...thank you!!

This is a very good recipe. I made this for my family and after reading many of the reviews that recommended adding a bit of honey, I did, too. This was excellent! Just the right amount of, heat & sweet to it. If you like it spicier I would say leave the honey out and possibly add a little more siracha-but honestly, it is great just the way it is with a little honey (about a TBSP). I used chicken breasts because that's what we like to grill and they were so tender and juicy. I doubled the recipe and had a lot of marinade left over. I added it to a sauce pan and boiled it for a few minutes on the stove. It thickened slightly, and I used it to continue basting the chicken as we grilled it. It gave it extra flavor. As I try recipes, my family lets me know if its a, "keeper" and this one definitely is a keeper!

GREAT MARINADE FAST TASTY I put chicken thighs in ziplock and this marinade. Froze. Easy to bring out and grill or slow cooker with cornstarch at end to thicken sauce. Great in slow cooker. Of all the soy sauce brown sugar type marinades, this is my favorite. The siriacha, chili, and others give it great flavor.
Takes a bit to make the marinade but the chicken thighs came out very tasty and carmelized nicely on the grill.

My fiancé raved about this one! I used chicken breasts.Doubled the sauce boiled thickened with corn starch poured over rice , along with grilled asparagus. Marinated for 7 hours, next time will be overnight. Definitely will be in the summer grill rotation 😋
Ohhhhh my i pulled this one off almost perfectly. Marinated over night. Used breast instead of thighs. But I did gooooood
Great flavors and great grill recipe. Serviced with a couple of AR recipes: Asian salad and cauliflower fritter. Great meal.

This was very easy to put together. I marinated bone-in chicken breasts and a couple boneless chicken breasts for eight hours, and then grilled them. It turned out beautifully. Put the thighs on direct heat first so the skin can get crispy and then cooked them all with indirect heat. This will become a family staple for grilled chicken!

I've been making this for several years and have played a little bit with the marinade ingredients. I've used few tablespoons of orange marmalade when I had no orange juice. Added Korean chili sauce for a bit more zing. It's always big hit in my home and is gone in no time. (This is a tasty preparation for chicken legs as well.) Just noticed the recipe mentions boiling the marinade for "about 1 minute" to sterilize and use as a sauce. Allrecipes (and every other site I looked at) recommends boiling meat marinades for at least FIVE minutes to kill dangerous bacteria before consuming as a sauce. Maybe this is overdoing it, but I'd err on the side of safe guts for all.
Prepared as written but used a whole cut-up chicken, bones & skin included. Delicious recipe! Thank you!!

I lived in an apartment after a divorce when I found this recipe. Let’s just say I made A LOT of friends every time I grilled at the pool. 

I paired it with thin sliced zucchini and squash in a salt/pepper/garlic seasoning, also grilled. 

I was the hit of the BBQ with it. I had to buy extra so I could feed the neighbors. This recipe is AMAZING. 

OJ, lemon juice and paprika contributed greatly. But recipe is amazing as is as well. 

Well done!
It was great definitely cook it again. Good the next day too. My husband was out in the dark with a lantern grilling the thighs but he said it was worth it.
